title: Routing + KV-prefetch playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Context:
- Quick scratchpad: capture ideas for a playbook that ties together routing policies + KV-prefetch strategies for typical Redwood workloads (chat, completion, embeddings).
- Goal: reduce tail latency and token cost without regressing quality. Give SRE/serving engineers a set of patterns and experiments to try.

Problem statements / pain points we've seen:
- Cold-cache spikes on conversational flows (long prefixes) causes 2–5x token cost and latency spikes.
- Simple routing -> cheaper models causes hallucination/regression for some prompt families.
- Autoscaling reacts too slowly for bursty prefix-heavy workloads.

High-level playbook sections (brainstorm):
1) Detection & classification
   - heuristics to tag requests that benefit from prefetch: long context, repeated user prompts, known templates (support replies, code generation).
   - lightweight fingerprint: first 200 tokens -> lookup frequency/hit-rate stats.
   - signal sources: route header (client hint), user-id history, eval prompt set matches.

2) Prefetch strategies
   - synchronous prefetch: on initial request, issue KV warm-read for common prefixes (used when client can tolerate small extra p99).
   - asynchronous prefetch: background prefetch based on user trajectory predictions (good for chat flows).
   - LRU vs frequency-based candidate selection (thresholds, TTLs).

3) Routing policies (routing + model variants)
   - primary model vs cost-model fallback: route to cheaper quantized variant if prefix-safe.
   - policy layers: region -> tier -> quality -> cost. Implement policy checks in admission filter.
   - safe-fallbacks: automatic rollback to primary if quality signals drop (eval or user-reported).

4) Metrics & quality checks
   - latency: p50/p95/p99 for first token and sustained generation.
   - cost: tokens per request, infra GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens by route.
   - quality: eval set similarity, dropout in top-k distribution, user-facing signal (rate of re-rolls).

5) Experiments to run (MVP list)
   - Exp A: KV-prefetch synchronous for top-50 prefixes for chat workloads on dedicated pool. Compare p95 latency and token cost vs baseline.
   - Exp B: Async prefetch for active sessions (predict next prefix). Measure additional cost vs reduced tail latency.
   - Exp C: Route-to-quantized model for requests with <10% eval-similarity-risk. Monitor quality regressions via auto-evals.

6) Rollout strategy
   - Canary on <5% traffic, synthetic replay, compare with shadow mode for 24h.
   - Gradual ramp: 5 -> 25 -> 50 -> 100% with automatic rollback on SLI breach.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute a cheap "prefix safety" score at admission time? (ML model vs heuristics)
- What are good default TTLs for KV entries across model sizes? (bigger models -> larger KV footprints)
- Storage/eviction policy implications for Dedicated vs Hosted (multi-tenant vs isolated GPU pools).
- How to correlate user-facing quality regressions to routing decisions automatically?

User stories (rough):
- As an SRE, I want a policy template that enables KV-prefetch for chat sessions so that p99 tail latency is reduced without increasing cost >10%.
- As an ML engineer, I want a safe route-to-quantized toggle so I can test cost-optimized variants on low-risk prompt families.
- As a product PM, I want dashboards showing quality drift attributable to routing/prefetch decisions so we can measure user impact.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP playbook):
- Provide a documented policy template (YAML) + server-side checks for admitting prefetch.
- Implement one async prefetch experiment and collect 2 weeks of metrics.
- Define automated rollback thresholds (p95 latency, eval-regression delta).

Experiment instrumentation plan (notes):
- Add per-request tags: prefetch_mode, route_variant, prefix_fingerprint.
- Store metrics in traces/observability with sampling for full payloads.
- Hook into Console: per-route p95 latency and quality signal charts.

Risks & mitigations:
- Over-prefetching increases cost: add budget guardrails and per-customer quota.
- Prefetch cache pollution: enforce frequency thresholds and prioritise active sessions.
- Quality regressions from cheaper variants: require shadow/eval pass before any ramp.

Quick action items (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Draft YAML policy template (me)
- [ ] Add request tagging in serving runtime (ticket: JIRA-4567)
- [ ] Implement a replay harness to test prefix candidates (reach out to replay infra)
- [ ] Set up dashboard prototype in Console with prefetch tags (ask Console team)

Notes to self: keep this as a messy scratchpad. Will convert to PRD after experiments. Ping Priya for policy corner cases and Zoe for eval harness integration.
